What to look for in leather trousers

  • Match your jacket. A 360° connection zip keeps your suit together in a crash — stick to one brand range where you can.
  • Knee and hip armour. CE Level 2 at the knees is the minimum; hip protectors matter in low-speed falls too.
  • Boot gaiters. Internal gaiters seal over your boots and stop rain running into your footwear.
  • Riding-position fit. Always try trousers seated — check the waist, knee articulation and length in your riding posture.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on leather trousers?

Our catalogue spans £149.99 to £449.95. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Held, Spidi, Rev'it, Furygan, Rebelhorn, RST. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.q: How much should I spend on leather trousers?
faq.a: Our catalogue spans £149.99 to £449.95. Budget picks under £150 like the RST Sabre CE cover the essentials, the £150 to £400 mid-range suits most UK sport tourers, and premium options above £400 such as the Held Grind 2 add lighter materials, refinement and longer-term durability.

faq.q: Leather or textile trousers for UK riding?
faq.a: Textile is the practical all-weather choice thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best slide protection for dry, spirited riding but is not waterproof. Many UK riders own both and reach for leather on dry days.

faq.q: Do I need a connection zip?
faq.a: A 360 degree connection zip keeps your trousers and jacket joined in a crash, preventing the two riding up and exposing your back. Stick to one brand range, such as RST or Rev'it, so the zips match reliably.

They should feel snug when seated, not standing, with the knee armour sitting over your kneecap in the riding position. Leather gives a little as it beds in, so avoid sizing up too far or the armour will migrate out of place.
